ROLE: observer
You review the results of an incident investigation. Write a short summary of what the latest results show, then update the list of hypotheses (at most 4, most likely first).

Root-cause categories:
- bad_deployment: a new release introduced a defect (errors begin right after a deploy)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: every database connection in the pool is in use, so requests wait
- slow_query_missing_index: a database query became slow (for example a missing index)
- downstream_timeout: a dependency the service calls is slow or unresponsive
- memory_leak_oom: memory grows until the process is killed (OOM) and restarts
- disk_full: a volume is full so writes fail
- expired_tls_cert: a TLS certificate expired so handshakes fail
- misconfiguration: a wrong environment variable, setting or feature flag
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: request volume far above capacity, causing rate limiting or load shedding
- cache_stampede_outage: the cache is down or emptied so everything falls through to the database

Each hypothesis has root_cause_category (one of the categories), rationale, and supporting_evidence_ids (only IDs that appear in the evidence below).

Reply with only JSON in this shape:
{"summary": "...", "hypotheses": [{"root_cause_category": "disk_full", "rationale": "...", "supporting_evidence_ids": ["L-0123"]}]}

Alert: payments-service: HTTP error rate above 5% for 5 minutes (since 05:44 UTC)
Alerting service: payments
Alert time: 2026-08-04T05:44:00Z
Data available from 2026-08-04T04:00:00Z to 2026-08-04T07:00:00Z

Evidence so far (the latest results are steps 4 onwards):
Step 1: metrics_query {"end": "2026-08-04T06:30:00Z", "metric": "error_rate_pct", "service": "payments", "start": "2026-08-04T05:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check error rate evolution for payments service)
  Result: M-041: Change detected at 2026-08-04T05:40:00Z: mean 0.41 before, 22.2 after (265.3 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-041] payments.error_rate_pct from 2026-08-04T05:00:00Z to 2026-08-04T06:30:00Z (19 points, 5-minute steps): min=0.28 max=22.32 mean=13.02 last=22.32; mean=13.02. Change detected at 2026-08-04T05:40:00Z: mean 0.41 before, 22.2 after (265.3 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-08-04T05:10:00Z = 0.28 (lowest); 2026-08-04T05:40:00Z = 22.16 (first point after the change); 2026-08-04T06:30:00Z = 22.32 (last); 2026-08-04T06:30:00Z = 22.32 (peak).
Step 2: metrics_query {"end": "2026-08-04T06:30:00Z", "metric": "cpu_pct", "service": "payments", "start": "2026-08-04T05:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check CPU usage for payments service)
  Result: M-038: No significant change detected in this range.
  [M-038] payments.cpu_pct from 2026-08-04T05:00:00Z to 2026-08-04T06:30:00Z (19 points, 5-minute steps): min=30.11 max=43.27 mean=38.46 last=38.37; mean=38.46. No significant change detected in this range. Notable points: 2026-08-04T05:15:00Z = 30.11 (lowest); 2026-08-04T05:40:00Z = 43.27 (peak); 2026-08-04T06:30:00Z = 38.37 (last).
Step 3: metrics_query {"end": "2026-08-04T06:30:00Z", "metric": "db_pool_in_use_pct", "service": "payments", "start": "2026-08-04T05:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check database connection pool usage for payments service)
  Result: M-039: No significant change detected in this range.
  [M-039] payments.db_pool_in_use_pct from 2026-08-04T05:00:00Z to 2026-08-04T06:30:00Z (19 points, 5-minute steps): min=23.73 max=35.38 mean=29.08 last=32.26; mean=29.08. No significant change detected in this range. Notable points: 2026-08-04T05:05:00Z = 23.73 (lowest); 2026-08-04T06:00:00Z = 35.38 (peak); 2026-08-04T06:30:00Z = 32.26 (last).
Step 4: log_search {"end": "2026-08-04T05:50:00Z", "query": "error", "service": "payments", "start": "2026-08-04T05:35:00Z"} (asked because: Search payments service logs around the time error rate increased to identify the root cause.)
  Result: 3 matching log lines.
Levels: WARN 3. Distinct templates: 1.
Most frequent templates:
  3 x request error rate above SLO window=<N>m

  [L-0294] 2026-08-04T05:43:25Z payments WARN request error rate above SLO window=5m
  [L-0314] 2026-08-04T05:48:25Z payments WARN request error rate above SLO window=5m
  [L-0323] 2026-08-04T05:49:54Z payments WARN request error rate above SLO window=5m

Previous hypotheses:
- bad_deployment: A sudden increase in error rates without resource saturation suggests a recently introduced software defect. (evidence: M-041, M-038, M-039)
- misconfiguration: Configuration changes can immediately elevate error rates without impacting CPU or database pool usage. (evidence: M-041, M-038, M-039)
- downstream_timeout: A dependency failure could cause payments service requests to fail abruptly. (evidence: M-041, M-038)
